headline: Turin founders building AI agents right now will own the next wave of European automation startups.
why_now: AI agents are exploding across GitHub (96 activity, 94 growth) and Hugging Face (92), with strong news coverage (88) and hiring demand (85). For a founder in Turin—where automotive, manufacturing, and industrial automation clusters are deep—this is a rare chance to combine frontier AI tooling with regional industry strengths before the market saturates.
study: Complete the Anthropic 'Building Effective Agents' course and replicate each pattern (router, ReAct, multi-agent) in a local repo.
Read the LangGraph and CrewAI docs end-to-end; build a 3-agent workflow that researches a topic, drafts a report, and critiques itself.
Study the Model Context Protocol spec; implement a custom MCP server exposing a Turin public-transport or port-of-Savona logistics API to an agent.
Clone and dissect 2 top starred agent repos from the past 90 days (filter by language you know); document architecture trade-offs in a public notes repo.
Take a short course on evals (e.g. LangSmith or DeepEval) and learn to measure agent reliability before shipping anything.

build.title: Turin Industrial Ops Agent
build.description: A multi-agent system that ingests unstructured supplier emails, maintenance logs, and sensor exports from a Turin-area manufacturing client, plans follow-up actions, calls internal APIs to update ERP/CMMS records, and emails a human supervisor with a confidence-scored summary. It demonstrates tool use, planning, fallback handling, and human-in-the-loop—exactly what European industrial buyers will pay for.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README and architecture diagram
5-minute Loom demo walking through a real supplier-email → ERP update flow
Technical write-up (1,500 words) on LinkedIn or your blog covering evals, failure modes, and cost per task
Live hosted demo on a free Render/Fly.io instance

publish: Post the write-up on Hacker News (Show HN) and LinkedIn with a hook aimed at Turin/Italian industrial operators; tag Politecnico di Torino AI labs and Italian AI communities.
Submit a 10-minute talk proposal to meetups like Torino AI, Codemotion Italy, and PyData Turin; offer a live demo.

Publish a short thread on X/Twitter and a cross-post in the Italian r/MachineLearning and local founder Slack/Discord groups, then DM 10 Turin-based CTOs at manufacturing scaleups offering a free pilot.
Open-source a small reusable piece—an MCP server or eval harness—and submit it to Hugging Face Spaces and awesome-agent lists for discoverability.
skills: LLM orchestration and agent design patterns
Evaluation, observability, and cost optimization of agent systems
Founder-level go-to-market for AI products in Italy
risks: Agent reliability is still brittle, and a flaky demo to industrial buyers can kill credibility—invest seriously in evals before any client pilot.
The space is moving so fast that frameworks you learn today may be obsolete in 6 months; prioritize transferable patterns over specific libraries.
confidence: High confidence—signals are strongly aligned with founder career goals, your local industrial ecosystem, and a market with proven willingness to pay.
